text:
marta: Spun up wytham9b (9B) int4 canary — seeing intermittent OOMs on microbatch 4/8 with max_new_tokens=256. Posting logs + config.

devon: same in CI repro... here's excerpt of kernel trace:
```
E2024-06-15T01:12:10Z OOM at alloc_page kernel_slot=23 size=12MB
KV cache entries=1200 slot_used=0.87
```

kevin: Hypothesis: scheduler is allocating large contiguous buffers -> fragmentation when prefetch+int4 combine. Try max_new_tokens=128 + microbatch=2 or enable slot_compactor/soft_reserve.

marta: Tried max_new_tokens=128, microbatch=2 -> OOMs dropped from 0.23% -> 0.01% but p95 latency went 8% up (220ms -> 238ms). Quality unchanged on quick eval.

alyssa: For int4 canaries we usually see KV churn. Recommend soft_reserve=true and kv_eviction_threshold=0.6, also set prefetch=false for warmstart window.

devon: Ran a patch: batching_policy=adaptive, max_batch_size=16, prefetch=false, soft_reserve=true.
Stress run 2k reqs: OOM=0, eviction_rate=0.12, p95=260ms. Memory fragmentation metric (frag_score) dropped from 0.72 -> 0.45.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout of wytham9b/int4 -> step 1/3 success

kevin: Also try 'prefix_cache' on routes with short prompts to reduce KV allocations; that helped on other 9B models.

marta: Plan: canary tonight with config: max_new_tokens=128, max_batch_size=16, soft_reserve=true, kv_eviction_threshold=0.6, prefetch=false. Will run full perf+quality harness. Flag if OOM > 0.05% or p95 > 350ms.

ops: :+1: Add alert: eviction_rate > 0.2, OOM_rate > 0.05%, frag_score > 0.6. Also tag the run 'wytham-int4-canary-june'

alyssa: One more: add per-layer quant sensitivity: fallback top-4 layers -> float16 if we see quality regression on long-form QA.

marta: thanks. I'll create the canary PR and attach benchmark link when ready.
